stances_toward.note: Chișinău claims the left bank as an integral part of Moldova and has a reintegration policy (the March 2026 non-paper: 'Moldova is the sole subject of international law', no special status, international civilian mission), but does not control the territory (about 11% of the national area), where about 1,500 Russian soldiers are stationed and Tiraspol's security services are commanded by FSB officers. Grade follows the ontology: claimed, not controlled. Moldova's present strategy is to wait for conditions on the left bank to become unsustainable while extending Moldovan law. Bond - grievance: the 1990 secession and the 1992 war.

stances_toward.note: Unrecognised even by Moscow, but garrisoned by it: about 1,500 troops of the Operational Group guard Cobasna, the security services are run by FSB officers, and the 2025 energy crisis after Ukrainian transit ended showed that the enclave lives on Russian gas Moscow chooses to send or not. Moscow's use is leverage on Chisinau - Sandu's proposal to fold the garrison into a Ukraine settlement was refused by her own minister as a Russian veto on the EU path. Ally de facto, no treaty. Bond - affinity: Russian-speaking, Soviet, a 'Russian world' outpost.

relations_to.summary: Chișinău claims the left bank (about 11% of its territory) and has a reintegration policy: peaceful, no special status, demilitarisation, an international civilian mission replacing the peacekeeping format, a 1+1 negotiating track and gradual extension of Moldovan fiscal, customs and trade law. There is no mechanism for the withdrawal of Russian troops; Sandu would prefer to join the EU 'in a single step' with the region and accepts joining without it if Russian forces block reintegration.

relations_to.summary: Moldovagaz is the legal gas supplier to the left bank until 31 Dec 2026: in winter the region needs up to 3.7 million cubic metres a day and received about 3 million in late 2025, less than 1.5 million in early October 2025. Hungary's MET Group buys the gas, payments pass through Dubai-registered intermediaries that have changed at least three times, and Russia finances it on credit.
relations_to.note: Carnegie records under 1.5 mcm/day in the first half of October 2025, before full supply was restored on 17 Oct 2025; Novaya Gazeta gives about 3 mcm/day for the winter.

relations_to.summary: Until 2024 the Cuciurgan plant (Inter RAO-owned, in Transnistria) produced the larger part of Moldova's electricity, and the existing connection to Romania still runs through Transnistrian territory; Moldova stopped buying its power in January 2025 and the Vulcănești-Chișinău 400 kV line (cost about EUR 27m, due end-2025) that would bypass it was still unfinished in June 2026.
relations_to.note: Radio Moldova (Dec 2024) says 60-80%; the IEŚ (May 2024) says 'almost entirely' but its shares do not add up; 0.7 is the midpoint of the 60-80% range and is our inference.
